correctness.rationale: Positive fixed points solve the two denominators-cleared conics. The five exact-rational brackets prove a positive continuous first nullcline and four alternating signs of the second; four disjoint intervals thus each contain a positive fixed point. The first conic is irreducible by an invertible affine coordinate change and nonzero constant product; strict second-nullcline sign differences exclude a shared conic. Bezout gives at most four intersections. Each is transverse since the four distinct points exhaust total intersection multiplicity four. The independent checker verify.py passed all rational comparisons; numerical quartic roots are diagnostic, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary paper proves the at-most-four conic bound but states that no four-positive-intersection example was located, then treats only cases with at most three (Section 3 after Theorem 3.2, equation (13)). The exact positive-parameter certificate now attains that sharp bound, which the primary text does not imply. Direct claim/alias comparisons with indexed mathematical records show nearby multiplicity results for different models and equations, not the claimed four intersections in this specific shared-parasite mixture. This is a best-knowledge priority assessment, not proof that no equivalent example exists elsewhere.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible follow-up could exhibit four positive intersections of the same system; no independence or priority certification is claimed.

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies the four-positive-equilibrium case as unobserved, so its actual attainability is a natural unresolved structural question. A positive rational witness with a strict sign margin resolves sharpness of the known bound and establishes a nonempty open parameter regime, enabling future study of competition outcomes. This is not simply a title change or recomputation of a known parameter table; no general ecological predictions or stability types are claimed.
